newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: S. Korea's Yukong mulls restart of refomer in May.
newsitem.headline: S. Korea's Yukong mulls restart of refomer in May.

text.p: South Korean Yukong Ltd is considering to restart its 8,000-barrel-per-day (bpd) reforming unit in May in anticipation of increased reformate demand in Japan, an industry source said on Friday.
Weak gasoline and petrochemical prices forced Yukong, the country's largest refiner to shut the unit on January 24 with plans to restart at the end of June.

Yukong has three reforming units, which processes naphtha into reformate for either gasoline blending or further production into petrochemical BTX. The reformers have a total capacity of around 60,000-bpd.
"With the bad economy, domestic gasoline demand is stagnant," the source said commenting on South Korean demand.
"But Yukong is considering starting its reformer in May...especially with Japanese demand for reformate expected to increase in the second quarter.
"Most (Japanese) refineries try to increase their inventories for the summer driving season but many refineries also have turnarounds and have to import reformate," he said.
Japanese refineries' annual maintenance shutdowns started in April and last as late as October, but are mainly concentrated in May and June, traders said.
They said Japan's monthly imports of four to five 100,000-barrel cargoes of reformate could be raised to as many as eight cargoes in May and June.
Latest data from Japan's Trade Ministry showed a total of 327,000 barrels were imported in March, down 25.7 percent from February.
"There are several requirements from Japanese refiners. After Golden Week, they will decide their position," a trader said. The Golden Week holidays in Japan last from end April to early May.
